messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v0.8.1 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi, aroma.affymetrix v0.8.1 is available.  With this update R v2.6.0
is now required.  Because of this move, in the next release I will be
able to clear out some old heavy BioC packages that are not used by
aroma.affymetrix but was "forced upon us" due to package dependencies
in previous BioC versions.  Here are the details:

Version: 0.8.1 [2007-12-01]
o DEPENDENCIES: Package now requires R v2.6.0 or newer.  The main reason
  for this is so we can move away from outdated package dependencies.
o NOTE: For AllelicCrosstalkCalibration and FragmentLengthNormalization,
  the default is now to exclude units/cells on sex chromosomes from
  the model fitting (in order not shrink XX and XY samples towards
  each other).  For instance, AllelicCrosstalkCalibration argument
  'subsetToAvg' defaults to '-XY' which automatically look up all units
  and then cells that are on ChrX and ChrY.  For this to work, there
  must be a genome information file for the chip type. Note, '-XY' will
  work also on chip types for which there are no ChrX, e.g. Mapping250K_Nsp.
  The output data set will be get the extra tag '-XY' whenever this
  type of subsetting is used.  To fit with all units, use 'subsetToAvg=NULL'.
o MODEL UPDATE: The AllelicCrosstalkCalibration method would,
  if 'targetAvg' was specified (default), rescale the probe signals
  such that the average of *each* allele-pair group would equal
  the target average (default =2200).  However, this approach would
  make it hard to correct for other kinds of systematic effects,
  e.g. varying mixing proportions of target DNA from different
  enzymes.  For instance, on the GenomeWideSNP_6 chip type the
  symptom could be that raw CN estimates for CN probes would be
  biased compared with SNP units.  The default, for these SNP & CN
  chip types ("5.0" & "6.0") is now to rescale all signals on the
  array together, i.e. basically a median scale normalization.  For
  the SNP only chip types ("10K", "100K" & "500K") the default is to
  rescale by group.
o UPDATE: Updated AffymetrixNetAffxCsvFile to recognize enzyme
  fragment annotation data for the new GenomeWideSNP_6 CSV files.
o BUG FIX: The multi-enzyme model implemented was not the one in mind;
  The correction for the multi-enzyme data points was not right.
  The example(normalizeFragmentLength) has been updated to also display
  the normalized log-ratios (as a function of fragment length as well
  as they densities).  That revealed the bug.  The example also tests
  the case for non-aliquot mixing proportions between enzymes. This
  is indeed "automagically" corrected for by the model itself, i.e.
  there is no need to estimate the mixing proportions explicitly.
o BUG FIX: The AllelicCrosstalkCalibration introduced in previous
  version was broken for 10K (and possibly also for 100K and 500K).
o TESTS: Added test script for HuEx-1_0-st-v2 by Elizabeth Purdom.
o CLEAN UP: Moved the following methods to R.utils: copyFile(),
  dataFrame(), isEof(), and reassignInPackage().
o CLEAN UP: normalizeAverage.{matrix,list}() is now instead in
  the aroma.light package.
o Package pass R CMD check on R v2.6.1 patched as well as all
  redundancy tests in testScripts/.

As always, see group page for details on how to update/install.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: exon array cdfs
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I just wanted to let people know that I have made cdfs corresponding
to the Affy annotation from Sept. 14, 2007 (corresponding to the
annotation with the NetAffx Affy software). The links are available on
under the 'Documentation on cdf types' in the pages for the exon
array. These cdfs have not been extensively tested; they do not,
however, have the replicate probe assignments that exist in the
previous cdfs (see documentation pages if this makes no sense to you).
And like the previous cdfs, the large control probesets are not
included.

Note: Affy released new annotation in November right after I finished
these cdfs(!) so these cdfs do not corresond to the latest annotation;
I am in the process of making the corresponding cdfs.

There is a cdf corresponding to core, extended and full probesets, as
well as two new cdfs: a cdf for main design probesets (so also free
and ambiguous probesets) and a cdf with only Affy designated control
probesets (but not necessarily the long ones from the full Affy that
have created problems) I have yet to explore what is here, but they
consist of things like genomic background probes, intron/exon probes
for housekeeping genes; etc. They should not correspond to grid
aligning probes, for example, but again I haven't check them.

Also, please contact me if you discover a problem in the cdf. These
should be considered 'beta' as I have not done extensive checking. I
don't know when I will be able to do this, so I decided to make it
available now.

Best,
Elizabeth

P.S. I have a program for taking a file with probeset annotation as to
what probeset goes with what gene/transcript cluster and converting
the default Affy cdf (with only exon probesets and no gene
definitions) into a gene and exon cdf. This does not reassign probes
to different probesets, so the exon definitions of Affy stay intact
for better or worse. If this of interest to you, please contact me via
the google group. If you want to start at the probe level and make
your own exon definitions, it is possible that someone has a program
for that too.

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Affy SNP 6.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On 04/12/2007, mbc...@gmail.com <mbc...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> Sorry I have been off this list for quite a while and not aware the
> latest update.
> It seemed like aroma.affymetrix is ready for Affy SNP 6.0 arrays....is
> it correct?

For CN analysis, yes (with the disclaimer that we are still optimizing
the method).  I've created a page describing how to proceed.  Please
see:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis-6-0

>  If I have two 6.0 arrays from the same person (1 tumor, 1 control),
> can I use this software to get
> copy number estimates for this person, using the control array as the
> reference?

I have only tried it with a minimum of six hybridizations, but in
theory it should work.  I've added some comments to the page on what
steps are single-chip and what steps are multi-chip methods.

I've also added some notes to the above document on how to do paired
CN segmentation.

> If I have the same paired arrays for multiple people, should I analyze
> each person (2 arrays)
> one time, or should I pool all the arrays together?

It is (almost) always the case that it is better to process arrays
together, especially when you have so few.  Also see my notes on which
methods are single-array methods and which are not.

Let me/us know how it goes.

Best,

Henrik

messages.subject: 64-bit installation error in sfit
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,

I just successfully installed aroma.affymetrix onto a 64-bit Solaris
10 system, and thought I would post what may be a bug in the
installation of "sfit" (and more importantly, the solution).

I have searched the archives, and Henrik mentioned that sfit shouldn't
install by default? This seems not to be the case. sfit is a
dependency of GLAM, and thus is required.

Because i'm using R-64bit, which was built from source, most new
packages that I install, that also require compilation manage to
retrieve the appropriate compiler/linker flags from an unkown (by me)
location. I think there's a config.site style of file somewhere that
contains the appropriate CC, CFLAGS, LDFLAGS etc variables that I set
when installing R. The most important flags (for compiling in 64-bit)
seem to be -m64 and -mcpu=v9

Using the suggested method of installing aroma.affymetrix (see below)
I was able to install all required packages except for sfit (and
GLAM), and I tracked the error down to the Makefile within the sfit
package, which does not realise that i'm trying to compile in 64bit,
ie doesn't find the appropriate installation options that nearly all
other packages that require compilation are able to find.

I installed using the recommended:

source("http://www.braju.com/R/hbLite.R")
hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix")

The error was:
    # * Installing to library '/usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/
library'
    # * Installing *source* package 'sfit' ...
    # ** libs
    # ** arch -
    # gcc -Wall -O3 -I/usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/include -I/
usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/include  -I/usr/local/include    -
fPIC  -g -O -m64  -mcpu=v9 -c cfit.c -o cfit.o
    # gcc -Wall -O3 -I/usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/include -I/
usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/include  -I/usr/local/include    -
fPIC  -g -O -m64  -mcpu=v9 -c spa.c -o spa.o
    # gcc -O3 cli.c cfit.o spa.o -o cfit -lm
    # ld: fatal: file cfit.o: wrong ELF class: ELFCLASS64
    # ld: fatal: File processing errors. No output written to cfit
    # collect2: ld returned 1 exit status
    # make: *** [cfit] Error 1
    # ERROR: compilation failed for package 'sfit'
    # ** Removing '/usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/library/sfit'

This error is because the compilation command "gcc -O3 cli.c cfit.o
spa.o -o cfit -lm" should be "gcc -O3 -m64  -mcpu=v9 cli.c cfit.o
spa.o -o cfit -lm"

The solution was (see two lines with ">>>"):
cat /tmp/RtmpZy5ZIi/downloaded_packages/sfit/src/Makefile
    # INCLUDES = ${HOME}/include
    # LIBS = ${HOME}/lib
>>> # CC = gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9
    #
    # all: cfit
    #         cp cfit dummy.so
    #         mv cfit ../inst/bin/
    #
    # cfit: cfit.o spa.o cli.c spa.h
>>> #         $(CC) cli.c cfit.o spa.o -o cfit -lm
    #
    # test: cfit dye2.dat
    #         cfit 5 dye2.dat -a .01 -d 1 --outM stdout -q 10 -Q 90
    #
    # clean:
    #         rm -f ../inst/bin/cfit
    #         rm -f dummy.so
    #         rm -f *.o
    #
    #
######################################################################
    # # HISTORY:
    # # 2006-05-20
    # # o Added a clean rule.
    # # o Added a rule to move the build binary to ../inst/bin/ when
done.
    # # 2006-05-16
    # # o Removed -liberty from gcc in cfit target. /HB
    #
######################################################################

Correct output is:
$ make
    # gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9  -c -o cfit.o cfit.c
    # gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9   -c -o spa.o spa.c
    # gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9 cli.c cfit.o spa.o -o cfit -lm
    # cli.c: In function `main':
    # cli.c:88: warning: 'f' might be used uninitialized in this
function
    # cp cfit dummy.so
    # mv cfit ../inst/bin/

Now that this can compile, i rebuilt the R package, and then installed
it as follows:
$ make clean
$ cd /tmp/RtmpZy5ZIi/downloaded_packages
$ R CMD build sfit
$ R CMD INSTALL sfit_0.1.5.tar.gz

Admittedly, I don't fully understand the magic that configure scripts
perform, and how installing R packages seems to find the correct
compiler/linker flags; however, it's clear the fairly simple Makefile
for sfit could benefit from finding these flags?

I hope this post helps users, and perhaps someone can let me know
where R finds its flags from under normal operation?

cheers,
Mark

Hi,
I have a question about manually giving your own tags in the analysis.
What I would *like* to do is  at different points in my analysis, use a
different cdf, and note this by putting a tag (I'm working on exon
arrays, so I have many I can choose from!). But this seems to overwrite
the default tag rather than append to it. For example, for BG
correction I do this:
csBGTissue<-RmaBackgroundCorrection(csTissue,tags="main") #indicating I used cdf with all 'main' design probesets

This appears to give me the folder "Affy_tissue_comm,main", not
"Affy_tissue_comm,RBC,main", which I would prefer. I'm assuming there's
not a way to do this, except manually change the folder name or tag,
then redefine csBGTissue using AffymetrixCelSet$fromFile (I might like
"appendTag" as well as 'tag' option on commands, but that seems a big
change...). So my question is to double check how this trickles down --
I haven't run the continuing analyzes yet and I'd like to know.
1) When I quantile normalize, I assume I will get a folder
"Affy_tissue_comm,RBC,main,QN", assuming I fix the tag for my
background correction

2) Then when I do my plm call, I'm going to switch to the 'core' cdf (a
subset of the probes in the 'main' cdf, so I'm assuming this won't
create any problems). So if I didn't add any further tags in my call,
I'd get a folder "Affy_tissue_comm,RCB,main,QN,RMA,merged" (because I'm
doing ExonRmaPlm). The following call,
ExonRmaPlm(csNTissue, mergeGroups=TRUE,tag="core")
will give me a folder "Affy_tissue_comm,core", which is not what I want, so I need to do
ExonRmaPlm(csNTissue, mergeGroups=TRUE,tag="RBC,main,QN,RMA,merged,core")

3) Then the FIRMA function seems to do something odd by default,
comparatively, though I have not rerun it since last spring, so please
correct me if this isn't current somebody, but it takes forever to run,
so I'd like to fix it upfront rather than run it and then correct it.
It makes a folder 'modelFirmaModel' at the level of 'plmData' and
'rawData', etc. Then under that it makes the folder
'"Affy_tissue_comm,FIRMA", removing my previous collection of tags. And
then the files are called 'xyz,FIRMAscores.cel'. That seems like an
awful lot of 'FIRMA'. Mark has already a beta function to rewrite a bit
of the firma functions to allow other options. I think its a good time
to update this as well. e.g. a folder 'scoresData' (so there might be
other scores for other chips, etc. that could go here), then at the
next level, keep all the previous tags as well as give a tag 'FIRMA',
then under that save all the .cel files for which ever of the possible
options, with informative filename tags, e.g. 'xyz,medResScores.cel'
and 'xyz,UQWtScores.cel' in the same folder. Feedback?

By the way, what if I was not working with cdfs that are subsets of
each other? Are the cells not contained in the cdf just left blank for
the various processes, or are the original values copied over?

Thanks,
Elizabeth

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] tags
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On 05/12/2007, Elizabeth Purdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>  I have a question about manually giving your own tags in the analysis. What
> I would *like* to do is  at different points in my analysis, use a different
> cdf, and note this by putting a tag (I'm working on exon arrays, so I have
> many I can choose from!). But this seems to overwrite the default tag rather
> than append to it. For example, for BG correction I do this:
>  csBGTissue<-RmaBackgroundCorrection(csTissue,tags="main")
> #indicating I used cdf with all 'main' design probesets
>
>  This appears to give me the folder "Affy_tissue_comm,main", not
> "Affy_tissue_comm,RBC,main", which I would prefer. I'm assuming there's not
> a way to do this, except manually change the folder name or tag, then
> redefine csBGTissue using AffymetrixCelSet$fromFile (I might like
> "appendTag" as well as 'tag' option on commands, but that seems a big
> change...). So my question is to double check how this trickles down -- I
> haven't run the continuing analyzes yet and I'd like to know.

There is a concept I call the "asterisk tag" allowing you to do:

csBGTissue <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(csTissue, tags=c("*", "main"))
print(getFullName(csBGTissue))
## [1] "Affymetrix-HeartBrain,RBC,main"

Using tags="*,main" should also do.  For most Transform:s and Model:s
there is an internal getAsteriskTag() method that are used to generate
the asterisk tag(s) given class, parameters etc.  I went through most
classes and made them utilize this, but it was not a complete scan,
for instance I avoided touching the exon classes since I knew you guys
were working on those.  Before a "*" tag was (as currently in
ExonRmaPlm) identified and set/replaced in the constructor function,
whereas you don't want to parse this until you actually query the
tags, e.g. via getTags() or otherwise.   I can do a 2nd scan through
all classes and update those - if so, make sure to commit what you
have and let me know when you're done.

>  1) When I quantile normalize, I assume I will get a folder
> "Affy_tissue_comm,RBC,main,QN", assuming I fix the tag for my background
> correction

Yes, every step is just appending tags.

>
>  2) Then when I do my plm call, I'm going to switch to the 'core' cdf (a
> subset of the probes in the 'main' cdf, so I'm assuming this won't create
> any problems). So if I didn't add any further tags in my call, I'd get a
> folder "Affy_tissue_comm,RCB,main,QN,RMA,merged" (because
> I'm doing ExonRmaPlm). The following call,
>  ExonRmaPlm(csNTissue, mergeGroups=TRUE,tag="core")
>  will give me a folder "Affy_tissue_comm,core", which is not what I want, so
> I need to do
>  ExonRmaPlm(csNTissue,
> mergeGroups=TRUE,tag="RBC,main,QN,RMA,merged,core")

As describe above, the idea is to do:

plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csNTissue, mergeGroups=TRUE, tags="*,core")
print(getFullName(plm))
## [1] "Affymetrix-HeartBrain,RBC,main,QN,RMA,merged,core"

However, the current implementation puts "merged" at the end (try):

## [1] "Affymetrix-HeartBrain,RBC,main,QN,RMA,core,merged"

This is going to be corrected when I do the above updated.  Let me know.

>
>  3) Then the FIRMA function seems to do something odd by default,
> comparatively, though I have not rerun it since last spring, so please
> correct me if this isn't current somebody, but it takes forever to run, so
> I'd like to fix it upfront rather than run it and then correct it.

I don't really see why FirmaModel should to be slower than in the
spring, but there might be updates and confounded effects causing
this.  Mark, have you noticed a slowdown?

However, one this I have noticed but haven't troubleshooted yet is
that with R v2.6.0 (or R v2.6.1) I noticed, on both Linux and Windows,
that when some calls return to the R prompt, some warning takes
awfully long to display (generate), e.g. if I have six arrays and get
six warnings that some NAs where generated in a log transform, each of
the take a very long time to display (and Ctrl-C does not work).  My
best guess this is something with R v2.6.x and not aroma.affymetrix,
but I might be wrong.  I haven't done thorough tests.

> It makes
> a folder 'modelFirmaModel' at the level of 'plmData' and 'rawData', etc.
> Then under that it makes the folder '"Affy_tissue_comm,FIRMA", removing my
> previous collection of tags.

The 'modelFirmaModel', called a "root path",  is specified in the
getRootPath() method, so you need to update getRootPath.FirmaModel().

In order to "pass down" tags from previous steps, you have to let
getTags() of FirmaModel to take care of this.  The current
implementation seems to only return the tags for FirmaModel, cf.
this$.tags.  I can update this to do the default, i.e. basically the
effect of "*,<new tags>".  Let me know.

> And then the files are called
> 'xyz,FIRMAscores.cel'. That seems like an awful lot of 'FIRMA'. Mark has
> already a beta function to rewrite a bit of the firma functions to allow
> other options. I think its a good time to update this as well. e.g. a folder
> 'scoresData' (so there might be other scores for other chips, etc. that
> could go here), then at the next level, keep all the previous tags as well
> as give a tag 'FIRMA', then under that save all the .cel files for which
> ever of the possible options, with informative filename tags, e.g.
> 'xyz,medResScores.cel' and 'xyz,UQWtScores.cel' in the same folder.
> Feedback?

This is a design issue and I've been thinking about making a similar
move for segmentation data.  Currently aroma.affymetrix provides to
segmentation methods via classes GladModel and more recently CbsModel.
 For historical reasons, GLAD estimates are stored in gladData/ and
CBS estimates in cbsData/, e.g.

 gladData/HapMap270,100K,CEU,ACC,-XY,+300,RMA,A+B,FLN/
 cbsData/HapMap270,100K,CEU,ACC,-XY,+300,RMA,A+B,FLN/

However, note I do *not* add tags GLAD and CBS.  Since more
segmentation methods will come around, I've been thinking of doing the
following instead:

 cnsData/HapMap270,100K,CEU,ACC,-XY,+300,RMA,A+B,FLN,GLAD/
 cnsData/HapMap270,100K,CEU,ACC,-XY,+300,RMA,A+B,FLN,CBS/

where 'cns' is short for "copy-number segmentation" (or something
similar).  However, I haven't made the move yet, because first of all
I want to be sure it is a good one before break peoples existing
folders (although manual renaming is not that hard so that existing
results will be automatically found).  On a more philosophical level
there is a design decision that has to be made, namely, should the
above two subdirectories hold identical file types or not?  In the
current setup, aroma.affymetrix know that all files found under
gladData/ is of a certain kind, and same for cbsData/.  If instead
cnsData/ is used, the file format has to be inferred from the tags -
and they you starting to add restrictions and information in the tags.
 It is important to think through consequences of such a move.

Before making the big move, one could keep the current root paths, but
add tags, e.g.

 gladData/HapMap270,100K,CEU,ACC,-XY,+300,RMA,A+B,FLN,GLAD/
 cbsData/HapMap270,100K,CEU,ACC,-XY,+300,RMA,A+B,FLN,CBS/

So at this stage I'm not sure if it "safe" to use the generic name
scoresData/ for everything.  I am happy to discuss it though (either
online or in person).

But I agree, it is better to make the big changes now before too many
people get affected.

>
>  By the way, what if I was not working with cdfs that are subsets of each
> other? Are the cells not contained in the cdf just left blank for the
> various processes, or are the original values copied over?

Are you asking about outputted CEL files?

For most (all?) cases where the output CEL file is of the same
dimension (nrow*ncol) as the input CEL file, the method createFrom()
of AffymetrixCelFile is used.  Two of the arguments it takes are
'methods=c("copy", "create")' and 'clear=FALSE' (default values).
Basically, the first one allows you to either do a file copy the
existing CEL file or create/build one from scratch.  If copying,
clear=TRUE will afterwards go and blank all CEL values (set them to
zero).  If "creating", the created CEL file is already blank, so
clear=FALSE will then read the data from the input file and write it
to the create file.  Thus, effectively, when clear=TRUE, the new CEL
will be blank and when clear=FALSE the new CEL will contain the same
values as the input file.  FYI, the createFrom() call is "atomic",
that is, if something fails or its interrupted during the call, there
will be no output file.  This is why it is safe to hit Ctrl-C almost
anytime.

In the case where chip-effect CEL files are created, they will always
be blank, because they are not created from a input CEL file but from
the CDF.

Hope this helps

Henrik

>
>  Thanks,
>  Elizabeth
>
>  >
>
>
>

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

thanks for reporting and troubleshooting this.

On 04/12/2007, mark_cowley <drco...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Dear list,
>
> I just successfully installed aroma.affymetrix onto a 64-bit Solaris
> 10 system, and thought I would post what may be a bug in the
> installation of "sfit" (and more importantly, the solution).
>
> I have searched the archives, and Henrik mentioned that sfit shouldn't
> install by default? This seems not to be the case. sfit is a
> dependency of GLAM, and thus is required.

I actually made 'sfit' part of the default installation two days ago.
The reason is that more and more people are using aroma.affymetrix for
CN analysis and 'sfit' is needed for allelic-crosstalk calibration,
which I recommend.

Sorry for my ignorance, but what is GLAM?  A package that utilizes the
'sfit' package?  I'm curious, what is GLAM used for?

>
> Because i'm using R-64bit, which was built from source, most new
> packages that I install, that also require compilation manage to
> retrieve the appropriate compiler/linker flags from an unkown (by me)
> location. I think there's a config.site style of file somewhere that
> contains the appropriate CC, CFLAGS, LDFLAGS etc variables that I set
> when installing R. The most important flags (for compiling in 64-bit)
> seem to be -m64 and -mcpu=v9

So, I know very little about R and 64-bit installation, for instance,
is R always installed as "64bit" on 64-bit *nix:es?  If so, we have
64-bit linux machines and 'sfit' installs out of the box.
Interestingly, when I build 'sfit' on these 64-bit machines, I do not
get the '-m64' flag, e.g.:

* Installing *source* package 'sfit' ...

** libs
** arch -
gcc -Wall -O3 -I/usr/local/linux/R-2.6.1/include
-I/usr/local/linux/R-2.6.1/include  -I/usr/local/include    -fpic  -g
-O2 -c cfit.c -o cfit.o
gcc -Wall -O3 -I/usr/local/linux/R-2.6.1/include
-I/usr/local/linux/R-2.6.1/include  -I/usr/local/include    -fpic  -g
-O2 -c spa.c -o spa.o

gcc -O3 cli.c cfit.o spa.o -o cfit -lm

cp cfit dummy.so
mv cfit ../inst/bin/
** R
** inst

This is here at stat dept in Berkeley, but I quite positive that when
I was at WEHI, Melbourne, they also had 64-bit machines.  When you
install/build R on a 64-bit Sun, do you have to specify this
explicitly?

What I am first trying to learn/conclude is whether this (the -m64
flag etc) is specific to Sun 64-bit systems, or not.

>
> Using the suggested method of installing aroma.affymetrix (see below)
> I was able to install all required packages except for sfit (and
> GLAM), and I tracked the error down to the Makefile within the sfit
> package, which does not realise that i'm trying to compile in 64bit,
> ie doesn't find the appropriate installation options that nearly all
> other packages that require compilation are able to find.

Your observation is correct, and does not surprise me, although I
cannot reproduce it.  The reason is that 'sfit' is quite special.  So,
the C code for 'sfit' were written by a P. Wirapati (WEHI at the time)
who did not use R but compiled code to executable.  So, he had a set
of command line tools that took certain arguments and read data from
file and wrote results back to file.  He had a Makefile for this.
What I've done, is basically to create R wrappers that write data to
temp file, calls his executables, and reads data back.  It is
basically lack of time (for 2+ yrs) that prevents me from writing R
.Call() wrappers to his C functions.  Anyone, help is always
appreciated ;)

More comments below.

>
>
> I installed using the recommended:
>
> source("http://www.braju.com/R/hbLite.R")
> hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix")
>
>
> The error was:
>     # * Installing to library '/usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/
> library'
>     # * Installing *source* package 'sfit' ...
>     # ** libs
>     # ** arch -
>     # gcc -Wall -O3 -I/usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/include -I/
> usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/include  -I/usr/local/include    -
> fPIC  -g -O -m64  -mcpu=v9 -c cfit.c -o cfit.o
>     # gcc -Wall -O3 -I/usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/include -I/
> usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/include  -I/usr/local/include    -
> fPIC  -g -O -m64  -mcpu=v9 -c spa.c -o spa.o
>     # gcc -O3 cli.c cfit.o spa.o -o cfit -lm
>     # ld: fatal: file cfit.o: wrong ELF class: ELFCLASS64
>     # ld: fatal: File processing errors. No output written to cfit
>     # collect2: ld returned 1 exit status
>     # make: *** [cfit] Error 1
>     # ERROR: compilation failed for package 'sfit'
>     # ** Removing '/usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/library/sfit'
>
> This error is because the compilation command "gcc -O3 cli.c cfit.o
> spa.o -o cfit -lm" should be "gcc -O3 -m64  -mcpu=v9 cli.c cfit.o
> spa.o -o cfit -lm"

So, what you observe below is that the R installer first search for
all native code (here *.c files) and uses *its* settings/options to
compile those.  This is why 'cfit.c' and 'spa.c' are compiles with the
' -m64 -mcpu=v9' flags that are specific to your system.  Then, R
looks for a Makefile and if it exists, it is called.  Since cfit.o and
spa.o already exists (built by R), 'make' goes to the rule:

cfit: cfit.o spa.o cli.c spa.h

	gcc -O3 cli.c cfit.o spa.o -o cfit -lm

which is called. Now, since this is hardwired in the package, you get
the above error.

>
> The solution was (see two lines with ">>>"):
> cat /tmp/RtmpZy5ZIi/downloaded_packages/sfit/src/Makefile
>     # INCLUDES = ${HOME}/include
>     # LIBS = ${HOME}/lib
> >>> # CC = gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9

Ok, this is where I am also a bit lost.  We basically want to insert
those R specific compiler options into the Makescript, but this should
be dynamic and not static.  Your solution (below) works if edited
manually.  So, something like:

CC = gcc -Wall -O3 ${RCCFLAGSHERE}

but I don't know the details.  Anyone, do you know if this is possible
and then where to grab the R compiler flags?

>     #
>     # all: cfit
>     #         cp cfit dummy.so
>     #         mv cfit ../inst/bin/
>     #
>     # cfit: cfit.o spa.o cli.c spa.h
> >>> #         $(CC) cli.c cfit.o spa.o -o cfit -lm

This line is simple and should have been there in the first place.

>     #
>     # test: cfit dye2.dat
>     #         cfit 5 dye2.dat -a .01 -d 1 --outM stdout -q 10 -Q 90
>     #
>     # clean:
>     #         rm -f ../inst/bin/cfit
>     #         rm -f dummy.so
>     #         rm -f *.o
>     #
>     #
> ######################################################################
>     # # HISTORY:
>     # # 2006-05-20
>     # # o Added a clean rule.
>     # # o Added a rule to move the build binary to ../inst/bin/ when
> done.
>     # # 2006-05-16
>     # # o Removed -liberty from gcc in cfit target. /HB
>     #
> ######################################################################
>
> Correct output is:
> $ make
>     # gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9  -c -o cfit.o cfit.c
>     # gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9   -c -o spa.o spa.c
>     # gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9 cli.c cfit.o spa.o -o cfit -lm
>     # cli.c: In function `main':
>     # cli.c:88: warning: 'f' might be used uninitialized in this
> function
>     # cp cfit dummy.so
>     # mv cfit ../inst/bin/
>
> Now that this can compile, i rebuilt the R package, and then installed
> it as follows:
> $ make clean
> $ cd /tmp/RtmpZy5ZIi/downloaded_packages
> $ R CMD build sfit
> $ R CMD INSTALL sfit_0.1.5.tar.gz

Ok, it is at least good that you can install 'sfit' this way.  Ideally
I would like to solve/understand how to do this, so if someone knows
more, please fill in.

>
> Admittedly, I don't fully understand the magic that configure scripts
> perform, and how installing R packages seems to find the correct
> compiler/linker flags; however, it's clear the fairly simple Makefile
> for sfit could benefit from finding these flags?
>
> I hope this post helps users, and perhaps someone can let me know
> where R finds its flags from under normal operation?

Hope this at least straightened out some of your question marks.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Henrik. The astrik tag is what I wanted. And I think Firma and
ExonRmaPlm function should be updated to do this inline with
everything else.

> plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csNTissue, mergeGroups=TRUE, tags="*,core")
> print(getFullName(plm))
> ## [1] "Affymetrix-HeartBrain,RBC,main,QN,RMA,merged,core"
>
> However, the current implementation puts "merged" at the end (try):
>
> ## [1] "Affymetrix-HeartBrain,RBC,main,QN,RMA,core,merged"
>

I do think it would be a little better to have 'merged' put before the
user tag, since it really modifies 'RMA' while the user tag modifies
the entire process of 'RMA,merged'.  I'm trying to set up tagging
rules for an aroma.affymetrix setup that will be shared between
people. So the added tag might also be someone's initials so it would
definitely be better at the end for that purpose. (On the other hand,
we may manually be entering new tags anyway, because we might want to
drop off the earlier initials for later steps and just have the
initials on the first entry of those series of tags to make the tags
easier to decipher...)

> I don't really see why FirmaModel should to be slower than in the
> spring, but there might be updates and confounded effects causing
> this.  Mark, have you noticed a slowdown?

I don't know if it is slower -- I meant to say that it was very slow
in the spring, so I haven't tried rerunning anything (bad grammer and
commas on my part). FIRMA might be better now. I think it was the
quantile() function, but it's hard to say.

I'm not tied to 'scoresData' and now that I read your explanation I
think that it is better to not depend too much on the tags -- what if
someone manually changes them or overrides them in their call to the
function? It's probably better to make folder names beyond the root
directory informative but not crucial. So I think I'd vote for keeping
each root folder for a different main method. I also think it's better
(for FIRMA) to keep the structure for another reason too; because we
plan to have the option to do variations of the summary statistic, so
it would be better to have

firmaData/Affy_tissue_comm,QN,RMA,merged,MEDRES/
firmaData/Affy_tissue_comm,QN,RMA,merged,UQWT/

rather than put these different scores in the same folder. That way,
if there is some further analysis, the tag 'MEDRES' will be kept and
moved on down.  This is also in line with the other folders, where the
root folder is the basic algorithm, and the subfolder distinguish
different options (at least for plmData for the exon arrays this is
the case). After all, you might have a lot of different folders there
just from different choices from previous steps that gave different
tags in addition to different datasets, and so it would get quickly
confusing. For example, my plmData folder looks like this,

plmData/Affy_tissue_comm,QN,RMA,merged/
plmData/Affy_tissue_comm,QN,RMA/
plmData/Affy_tissue_comm,RBC,QN,RMA,merged/
plmData/Affy_tissue_comm,RBC,QN,RMA/
plmData/BCGC_2006,QN,RMA,merged/
plmData/BCGC_2006,QN,RMA/

and once we add the option for multiple summary statistics in the
Firma folder, it will be similar, if not worse. Granted, I don't have
to do much with these, but still one less tag to decifier when I
decide which ones to zip up would be good!

I think that the cel files that save the scores should have a tag
"xyz, chip-by-exonScores.CEL" or something similar (maybe more
compact) that is not related to the method but to the format/size of
the information in the file; then every method that gives a score per
exon and chip (as oppose to per gene) has the same tag on the CEL
file. And gene scores could be 'chipScores', like 'chipEffects' in
plmData, though that's not really what we're doing but maybe with U133
that would be relevant.

Best,
Elizabeth

two questions:

normalization
using all these arrays together distort/bias the CN estimates? Why not
use only tumor or control
arrays? Similarly, if we expect very different CNs between people, is
it justifiable to pool all
the arrays across people together?

On 07/12/2007, mbc...@gmail.com <mbc...@gmail.com> wrote:
>

> I just read your page on CN analysis for 6.0 arrays and have
> two questions:
>
> 1) Should normalization come after summarization?

There are many different types of calibration and normalization.  The
steps given in the online description:

 http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis-6-0

is in the order I recommend.

Basically, the way I think about calibration/normalization is that
they remove systematic effects introduced at *different* steps of the
assay, and you have to work yourself *backwards* in order to remove
steps.  That is, if the PCR introduces artifacts and then additional
artifacts are introduced in the hybridization, you first have to
estimate and removed the hybridization artifacts before you can
"reach" ones from the PCR.  If you look at the above outline, that is
exactly the order things are done.  So, there are many different steps
of calibration/normalization, not just a "magic" one solving all
problems.

> 2) It seems like only the normalization step is multi-array, while
> others are
> single-array. But since normalization is the last step, is it correct
> that i still need
> to include all the arrays from the very beginning?

When you say "normalization" you mean the "PCR normalization" step,
correct?   Basically, whenever there is a multi-chip
calibration/normalization/summarization, you need all data to get best
results.  As a rule of thumb I always recommend to process all arrays
together.  If you have a lot of arrays, say 100s or 1,000s, then it
may be alright to process them in subsets.

> My concern is:
> if we expect very different CNs betweem tumors and controls, will
> normalization
> using all these arrays together distort/bias the CN estimates? Why not
> use only tumor or control
> arrays? Similarly, if we expect very different CNs between people, is
> it justifiable to pool all
> the arrays across people together?

This is a concern that is always raised and important.  However, since
we are using robust estimates as much as possible we can indeed have
quite a few "outliers" (tumors) without them affecting the estimate
and the end results.  I've processed several tumor data sets where I
pooled everything together.  See also the tumor/normal demo for
ChromosomeExplorer available on the main page:

  http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/

It is a paired analysis of 9 tumor/normal pairs and everything was
processed together all the way until created raw CNs as log2-ratios of
tumor over normal.

I recommend you to run the analysis and look at your results.  If you
at any random locus have a majority of samples being normal, things
should be alright.

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v0.8.2 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

aroma.affymetrix v0.8.2 is available.  The main improvement is better
and more consistent support for tags in how to locate files or sets
based on tags, but also how tags are appended automatically by some of
the transforms and some of the models.  I can see two backward
compatibility "issues" from these "tag" updates, but the workaround is
very simple.  I will post a separate message about this.

Version: 0.8.2 [2007-12-10]
o Added argument 'cdf' to static fromName() of AffymetrixCelSet.
  When using this argument, the 'chipType' argument is optional,
  and the returned CEL set will be using the specified CDF.
o In general, there is now better support for tagged CDFs.  For
  instance, AffymetrixCdfFile$fromName("HuEx-1_0-st-v2", tags="core")
  can be used to locate 'HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core.CDF'.
o UPDATE: Now output sets of a FirmaModel are stored in firmaData/.
  Previously they were stored under modelFirmaModel/.
o UPDATE: Updated AffymetrixNetAffxCsvFile and AromaUflFile to
  better import fragment-length information from NetAffx files.
o ROBUSTNESS: Now getGenomeInformation() of AffymetrixCdfFile asserts
  that the located GenomeInformation annotation file is compatible
  with the CDF.  Same for getSnpInformation().  Currently this can
  only be asserted for UGP & UFL annotation files.
o CONSISTENCY: Now getChipEffectSet() of ProbeLevelModel infers the
  monocell CDF from the CDF of the input data set and uses that when
  retrieving the chip-effect CEL set, not only when creating the set
  from scratch, but now also overriding the CDF according to the CEL
  header of existing sets.  In other words, if the CDF is overridden
  for the input data set, it will also be overridden (with the
  corresponding monocell CDF) in the chip-effect set.
o CLEAN UP: Went through all classes where applicable and updated
  so that getTags() and getAsteriskTags() work properly.  The
  latter was also renamed from getAsteriskTag() to getAsteriskTags()
  to indicate that it can actually return a multiple tags.
o CLEAN UP: Since much of the feature we used in 'affyPLM' moved to
  'preprocessCore', packages 'affyPLM' (and 'affy') are no longer
  required by default.  As with 'gcrma', the 'affy' package is only
  "suggested" and will be requested if need, e.g. when doing using
  one of background correction methods.
o DEVEL: Renamed all getAsteriskTag() methods to getAsteriskTags().
o BUG FIX: Tags from the input data set of FirmaModel were lost.

See group page for details on how to update/install.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: How to rename data-set tags such that previous results are still found
messages.subject_clean: How to rename data-set tags such that previous results are still found
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

with aroma.affymetrix v0.8.2 a few updates where made in how and what
tags are appended to output data sets.  These updates will in some
cases cause aroma.affymetrix not to find previously process data,
because it looks for directory names where the tags are in a different
order.  The solution is simply to rename all coinsurances to meet
these newer tags.

Here are a few cases where I can see you have to manually rename
directories.  You might experience other cases.  Basically, if you
find that your running the same script but aroma.affymetrix is not
finding the results, use verbose output and look where
aroma.affymetrix is searching now and rename your old results
accordingly.  Here are some examples showing you how to avoid
reprocessing:

1) COPY-NUMBER ANALYSIS:
If you previously did something like:

 plm <- AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE,
tags=c("+300", "*"))
 plm$shift <- +300;

the output data set would be something like:

   plmData/Foo_2007,ACC,-XY,+300,AVG/

Two things, now you should just do:

 plm <- AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE shift=+300)

and the output data set would become:

   plmData/Foo_2007,ACC,-XY,AVG,+300/

Note the reordering of the last two tags.  Thus, if you want to the
new code to detect you previously processed results, you should rename
all directories by swapping tags '+300,AVG' to 'AVG,+300' in all
occurrences in plmData/, gladData/, cbsData/, and reports/.  If not,
aroma.affymetrix will just reprocess you data.

2) EXON ANALYSIS:
If you previously did something like:

 plm <- ExonRmaPlm(cs, mergeGroups=TRUE, tags=c("*", "main"))

the output data set would previously be something like:

   plmData/Foo_2007,RBC,QN,RMA,main,merged/

whereas in the new version the 'merged' tag comes after RMA, i.e.

   plmData/Foo_2007,RBC,QN,RMA,merged,main/

This only applies if you explicitly added an extra tag as above, but
otherwise not.  For the same reason as above, you should then go
through all directories an rename the dataset directories from having
tags 'RMA,main,merged' to 'RMA,merged,main'.

3a) FIRMA ANALYSIS:
Previously FIRMA estimates would output data to root directory
modelFirmaModel/.  Now its output ends up in firmaData/.  Just rename
root directory modelFirmaModel/ to firmaData/.

3b) FIRMA ANALYSIS:
Previously the FIRMA model would drop tags from the input data set (a
mistake), e.g. the output would be

  modelFirmaModel/Foo_2007,FIRMA/

whereas now it is something like:

  firmaData/Foo_2007,RBC,QN,RMA,merged,FIRMA/

You should rename your old FIRMA data sets so that the have the proper tags.

Finally, note that some results cached to file (in ~/.Rcache/) will be
reprocessed.  There is no workaround for this, but they are on the
other hand "one timers".

Hope this helps

/Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I had a question about readCdfGroupNames(). There is a logical option
'truncateGroupNames' which the help says indicates 'whether unit names
should be stripped from the beginning of group names'. This makes it
sound like otherwise, the unit name is pasted to EVERY group name in
some way.

But in practice, I think this seems to operate only if the group name
matches the unit name and otherwise have no effect. In the case that the
group name matches the unit name, if option is T, it returns "" as the
group name and if F it returns the group name (which is same as the unit
name). This is indeed what I want, but I want to check that I am not
incorrect.

Thanks,
Elizabeth

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

Ok, this is an affxparser specific question, so in future please post
those to the Bioconductor list.

On 11/12/2007, Elizabeth Purdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I had a question about readCdfGroupNames(). There is a logical option
> 'truncateGroupNames' which the help says indicates 'whether unit names
> should be stripped from the beginning of group names'. This makes it
> sound like otherwise, the unit name is pasted to EVERY group name in
> some way.
>
> But in practice, I think this seems to operate only if the group name
> matches the unit name and otherwise have no effect. In the case that the
> group name matches the unit name, if option is T, it returns "" as the
> group name and if F it returns the group name (which is same as the unit
> name). This is indeed what I want, but I want to check that I am not
> incorrect.

Yes, if the unit name is a prefix of a group name, and
truncateGroupNames=TRUE (default), then that prefix is excluded.  For
example, if unit name is 'SNP_A-0923020' and the group name is
'SNP_A-0923020A', then the returned group name is 'A' if
truncateGroupNames=TRUE, and 'SNP_A-0923020A' if
truncateGroupNames=FALSE.

If I recall it correctly, the reason for adding this in the first
place was that for the same public SNP data stored as binary and as
ASCII would return different group names.  In the binary format, the
group names where simply 'A', 'C', 'G', or 'T' (indicating the
allele), whereas when stored in ASCII format the group names had the
unit name appended.  By making truncateGroupNames=TRUE by default the
user had one less thing to worry about.  I looked at the logs, and Ken
added this argument to the affxparser v1.7.5, because before it was
hardwired to TRUE, cf.

Version: 1.7.5 [2007-03-08]
o Added argument 'truncateGroupNames' to readCdfGroupNames()
  which defaults to TRUE for backward compatibility.  When
  TRUE, any prefix of group names identical to the unit name
  will be stripped of the group names.

So, it looks like you're walking down the same exon-array path as him.

Speaking of it, I think we "forgot" to provide the same feature for
readCdfUnits(), so you probably have spotted an inconsistency.

/Henrik

> > matches the unit name and otherwise have no effect. In the case that the
> > group name matches the unit name, if option is T, it returns "" as the
> > group name and if F it returns the group name (which is same as the unit
> > name). This is indeed what I want, but I want to check that I am not
> > incorrect.
>
> Yes, if the unit name is a prefix of a group name, and
> truncateGroupNames=TRUE (default), then that prefix is excluded.  For
> example, if unit name is 'SNP_A-0923020' and the group name is
> 'SNP_A-0923020A', then the returned group name is 'A' if
> truncateGroupNames=TRUE, and 'SNP_A-0923020A' if
> truncateGroupNames=FALSE.

> place was that for the same public SNP data stored as binary and as
> ASCII would return different group names.  In the binary format, the
> group names where simply 'A', 'C', 'G', or 'T' (indicating the
> allele), whereas when stored in ASCII format the group names had the
> unit name appended.  By making truncateGroupNames=TRUE by default the
> user had one less thing to worry about.  I looked at the logs, and Ken
> added this argument to the affxparser v1.7.5, because before it was
> hardwired to TRUE, cf.

> readCdfUnits(), so you probably have spotted an inconsistency.

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Someone showed me some example code that is posted online for lbl (not
on the group pages) to get a ngene x nchip matrix of the expression
values from a ExonRmaPlm fitting and it has a serious mistake. I don't
know where the code came from or who might be using it, so I thought I'd
point it out on the list. The code is roughly,

plm <- ExonRmaPlm(cs, mergeGroups=TRUE);
ces <- getChipEffects(plm);
chipEffectMatrix <- getData(ces, indices=NULL, "intensities")$intensities
cdf <- getCdf(ces);
groupNames <- readCdfGroupNames(cdf$.pathname, truncateGroupNames=FALSE);
chipEffectMatrix <- chipEffectMatrix[1:length(unlist(groupNames)),];

I just wanted to point out that this will not give the chip (gene)
effects, which is quite clear if you look at the first few lines of the
matrix.

The main mistake is in the last line, (though I can't vouch for the
other without double-checking it). In general, the 'getData' function
pulls data from every cell on the .CEL file as defined by the
corresponding cdf. The chip effects have a cdf (called a 'monocell' cdf)
that has a reduced number of cells, only 1 cell (entry) per every group
per unit on the original cdf, rather than per probe. For the ExonRmaPlm,
when mergeGroups=T only one value is needed per unit, so only one group
per unit has a value and the rest are zero. The last line of the above
code tries to get rid of these zero entries, but it is not that simple
since the nonzero ones are not the first ngene rows of the matrix.

Generally, I'm always a bit hesitant to use functions that need the
indices without extreme care because I don't think that the indices must
always go in the order of the units (except for the monocell, isn't the
index the position on the array of the probe, irrelevant to the
group/unit definitions?). In which case, getData would give you a matrix
with no way of mapping back to the names. However, the monocell is more
standard since its created by aroma.affymetrix for the sole purpose of
holding chip effects and is based on the cdf, not the probe positions;
just looking at the first few entries, it seems like the monocell might
have the indices and units that line up in the same order. In which case
this code could probably be fixed if instead it used
readCdfNbrOfCellsPerUnitGroup() and calculated the appropriate index in
that way. I'd stick with readUnits(), however and collapse the list
structure into a matrix (something I was thinking of coding myself since
I don't know of a function that does it, or maybe writing code based on
getData that made sure everything lined up and gave the names, because I
think getData would be faster).

The code above should give exon summaries, if plm was from
mergeGroups=FALSE, but then it would have the same issues of mapping
from indices to units/groups. If the monocell is in the 'right' order,
then the code would give the entries in the same order as
unlist(groupNames), so you could map back to the probeset ids in that way.

As a development question, if you want such a collapsed matrix for a set
of units, would it be faster to look up the appropriate indices (with
getCellIndices) and then use getData, or use readUnits and then use
matrix() on the output of unlist()? (Obviously for the chip effects,
this would have to be adjusted for the zeros, and readUnits leaves them
out automatically so that is more convenient)

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

does the following do what you want?  Example with SNP 500K chip
types, but the same should apply to exon arrays:

units <- 104:105;

# Total copy number => one chip effect per unit
plmA <- RmaCnPlm(cs, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE);
fit(plmA, units=units);
cesA <- getChipEffectSet(plmA);

# Allele- and strand specific estimate => one chip effect per unit group
plmB <- RmaCnPlm(cs, mergeStrands=FALSE, combineAlleles=FALSE);
fit(plmB, units=units);
cesB <- getChipEffectSet(plmB);

thetaA <- extractMatrix(cesA, units=units, returnUgcMap=TRUE);
print(thetaA);
##      CCL-256.1D CCL-256D CRL-2314D
## [1,]   970.8192 1271.880  1284.305
## [2,]   849.5079 1182.221  1088.414
## attr(,"unitGroupCellMap")
##   unit group cell
## 1  104     1  335
## 2  105     1  337

thetaB <- extractMatrix(cesB, units=units, returnUgcMap=TRUE);
print(thetaB);
##      CCL-256.1D  CCL-256D CRL-2314D
## [1,]  222.60452  289.8059  314.5850
## [2,]  755.66431  969.1988  966.5847
## [3,]  256.51810  416.1275  449.6467
## [4,] 1062.88782 1609.7344 1225.3984
## [5,]   63.16645  109.4760  139.5278
## [6,]  246.93521  284.7016  327.9100
## attr(,"unitGroupCellMap")
##   unit group cell
## 1  104     1  335
## 2  104     2  336
## 3  105     1  337
## 4  105     2  338
## 5  105     3  339
## 6  105     4  340

I think the attribute name speaks for itself.  You might prefer the following:

> dataB <- cbind(attr(thetaB, "unitGroupCellMap"), thetaB);
> dataB
##   unit group cell CCL-256.1D  CCL-256D CRL-2314D
## 1  104     1  335  222.60452  289.8059  314.5850
## 2  104     2  336  755.66431  969.1988  966.5847
## 3  105     1  337  256.51810  416.1275  449.6467
## 4  105     2  338 1062.88782 1609.7344 1225.3984
## 5  105     3  339   63.16645  109.4760  139.5278
## 6  105     4  340  246.93521  284.7016  327.9100

The reason for not "announcing" the above, is that I haven't decided
if the 'thetaB' or the 'dataB' structure should be returned by
extractMatrix(..., returnUgcMap=TRUE).  Note that 'thetaB' is a double
matrix (and the map attribute is a data frame), whereas 'dataB' needs
to be a data frame.  Comments?

So, of course, I found a bug in the code that had to be fixed.
Install the patch and the above should work for you;

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Affy SNP 6.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

my bad.  While trying to increase the robustness of custom CDFs it
seems like I managed to introduce a bug.  The quick solution is for
you to call:

> createMonoCell(cdf, verbose=verbose)

You should see something like:

20071211 23:18:44|Creating monocell CDF...
20071211 23:18:44| Chip type: GenomeWideSNP_6,Full
20071211 23:18:45| Output pathname (temporary): C:/Documents and Settings/hb/My
Documents/My Data/annotationData/chipTypes/GenomeWideSNP_6/GenomeWideSNP_6,Full,
monocell.CDF.tmp
20071211 23:18:45| Number of cells per group field: 1
...

and so on.  This will generate a so called monocell CDF out of the
main CDF and but it under annotationData/chipTypes/GenomeWideSNP_6/
for future usage.  This process takes quite a while, but is a one
timer.  When the monocell CDF is created, you should be able to
continue your analysis, i.e. from fit(plm, verbose=verbose) and so on.

I'll try to fix a patch by tomorrow so that fit() will automatically
call createMonoCell(), if missing.  FYI, I do run (18 hours)
redundancy tests between releases, but this one was not caught because
the test system already had the monocell created.

Cheers

Henrik

should detect that the monocell CDF is missing and then create it.

> On 11/12/2007, Elizabeth Purdom <epur...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>
>
> > Hello,
>
> > Someone showed me some example code that is posted online for lbl (not
> > on the group pages) to get a ngene x nchip matrix of the expression
> > values from a ExonRmaPlm fitting and it has a serious mistake. I don't
> > know where the code came from or who might be using it, so I thought I'd
> > point it out on the list. The code is roughly,
>
> > plm <- ExonRmaPlm(cs, mergeGroups=TRUE);
> > ces <- getChipEffects(plm);
> > chipEffectMatrix <- getData(ces, indices=NULL, "intensities")$intensities
> > cdf <- getCdf(ces);
> > groupNames <- readCdfGroupNames(cdf$.pathname, truncateGroupNames=FALSE);
> > chipEffectMatrix <- chipEffectMatrix[1:length(unlist(groupNames)),];
>
> > I just wanted to point out that this will not give the chip (gene)
> > effects, which is quite clear if you look at the first few lines of the
> > matrix.
>
> > The main mistake is in the last line, (though I can't vouch for the
> > other without double-checking it). In general, the 'getData' function
> > pulls data from every cell on the .CEL file as defined by the
> > corresponding cdf. The chip effects have a cdf (called a 'monocell' cdf)
> > that has a reduced number of cells, only 1 cell (entry) per every group
> > per unit on the original cdf, rather than per probe. For the ExonRmaPlm,
> > when mergeGroups=T only one value is needed per unit, so only one group
> > per unit has a value and the rest are zero. The last line of the above
> > code tries to get rid of these zero entries, but it is not that simple
> > since the nonzero ones are not the first ngene rows of the matrix.
>
> > Generally, I'm always a bit hesitant to use functions that need the
> > indices without extreme care because I don't think that the indices must
> > always go in the order of the units (except for the monocell, isn't the
> > index the position on the array of the probe, irrelevant to the
> > group/unit definitions?). In which case, getData would give you a matrix
> > with no way of mapping back to the names. However, the monocell is more
> > standard since its created by aroma.affymetrix for the sole purpose of
> > holding chip effects and is based on the cdf, not the probe positions;
> > just looking at the first few entries, it seems like the monocell might
> > have the indices and units that line up in the same order. In which case
> > this code could probably be fixed if instead it used
> > readCdfNbrOfCellsPerUnitGroup() and calculated the appropriate index in
> > that way. I'd stick with readUnits(), however and collapse the list
> > structure into a matrix (something I was thinking of coding myself since
> > I don't know of a function that does it, or maybe writing code based on
> > getData that made sure everything lined up and gave the names, because I
> > think getData would be faster).
>
> > The code above should give exon summaries, if plm was from
> > mergeGroups=FALSE, but then it would have the same issues of mapping
> > from indices to units/groups. If the monocell is in the 'right' order,
> > then the code would give the entries in the same order as
> > unlist(groupNames), so you could map back to the probeset ids in that way.
>
> > As a development question, if you want such a collapsed matrix for a set
> > of units, would it be faster to look up the appropriate indices (with
> > getCellIndices) and then use getData, or use readUnits and then use
> > matrix() on the output of unlist()? (Obviously for the chip effects,
> > this would have to be adjusted for the zeros, and readUnits leaves them
> > out automatically so that is more convenient)
>
> > Best,
> > Elizabeth

Those warnings are alright.  They just say that there are some loci in
some samples out of the 1.8 million loci across all samples that ended
up as missing value in the estimate.  This is likely due to the fact
that when you do cross-talk calibration a few loci will get a
non-positive probeset sum.

>
> Now I have the cesN object. How can I get the log2 expression values
> and chrosomsome location
> for each SNP and CNV? Is there any plotting function that I can use to
> visualize the data?

First, continue with the segmentation step.  You can view the results
in the ChromosomeExplorer (which will also provide a link to a tabular
file containing identified regions).

There is no method available for studying CN polymorphism (aberrations
common in the population).  All available methods right now are
identifying regions on a sample by sample case.

If you really want to get the raw CN for a set of SNPs (units), and
not just run the segmentation and identify regions, let me know.

> > cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("HapMap270,6.0,CEU,testSet", cdf=cdf)

>

Nope, the example online is correct.  It looks like you have
misunderstood how and where to put your data.  I *strongly* recommend
that you look at the online setup pages again, and don't continue
further before understanding the setup.  You need to differentiate
between annotation data and raw data, i.e. the former goes under
annotationData/ with a certain structure that is totally unrelated to
sample data, and the latter goes under rawData/ with a different
structure that is very much related to each of your experiments.

Right now, for your data when you do print(cesN) or getName(cesN), I
am quite sure the name reported is "chipTypes", which is not what you
want.  When you got your rawData/ setup correctly, you can replace the
prefix "chipTypes" with "HapMap270,6.0,CEU,testSet" (or whatever your
the name of the dataset you have) in all occurrences in probeData/ and
plmData/ (and cbsData/ if you got that far).

Cheers

Henrik

Hi,

> Those warnings are alright.  They just say that there are some loci in
> some samples out of the 1.8 million loci across all samples that ended
> up as missing value in the estimate.  This is likely due to the fact
> that when you do cross-talk calibration a few loci will get a
> non-positive probeset sum.
>

Yelp, I knew those warnings are not a concern.

> > Now I have the cesN object. How can I get the log2 expression values
> > and chrosomsome location
> > for each SNP and CNV? Is there any plotting function that I can use to
> > visualize the data?
>
> First, continue with the segmentation step.  You can view the results
> in the ChromosomeExplorer (which will also provide a link to a tabular
> file containing identified regions).
>
> There is no method available for studying CN polymorphism (aberrations
> common in the population).  All available methods right now are
> identifying regions on a sample by sample case.
>
> If you really want to get the raw CN for a set of SNPs (units), and
> not just run the segmentation and identify regions, let me know.

Yes, I really want those log2 values and locations for all the SNPs
and CNVs.
I think if I have the log2 values, I can calculate the CN by doing
log2(tumor)-log2(control).

> Nope, the example online is correct.  It looks like you have
> misunderstood how and where to put your data.  I *strongly* recommend
> that you look at the online setup pages again, and don't continue
> further before understanding the setup.  You need to differentiate
> between annotation data and raw data, i.e. the former goes under
> annotationData/ with a certain structure that is totally unrelated to
> sample data, and the latter goes under rawData/ with a different
> structure that is very much related to each of your experiments.

I see. Sorry about that....my mistake. I got the codes ran without any
problem so
thought I had set up these files correctly. I don't think it affected
the result, did it?
I will have a closer look of your setup pages soon.

Yes, that was what I got.

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I just did a doEverything() call (code by Mark Robinson, thanks very
much).   I have 12 Mouse ST arrays.  The call took 3.76 hrs, nearly
all of this time was due to the fit(plm) step (plm is the output from
RmaPlm).  Does that seem like a usual length of time to anyone?

 Total time for all units across all 12 arrays: 13522.67s == 225.38min
 Total time per unit across all 12 arrays: 0.38s/unit
 Total time per unit and array: 31.7ms/unit & array
 Total time for one array (35512 units): 18.78min = 0.31h
 Total time for complete data set: 225.38min = 3.76h
 Fraction of time spent on different tasks: Fitting: 99.3%, Reading:
0.1%, Writing: 0.6% (of which 75.19% is for encoding/writing chip-
effects), Explicit garbage collection: 0.0%

Here is the version of doEverything:

doEverything<-function(name,chip,checkChipType=FALSE,

doExon=FALSE,doCore=FALSE,force=FALSE,doMerge=FALSE,doResiduals=FALSE,
 doWeights=FALSE,getExpression=FALSE,verbose=Arguments$getVerbose(-8))
{

   cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chip,
checkChipType=checkChipType)
   if (doCore)
     chip<-paste(chip,",core",sep="")
   cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chip)
   setCdf(cs, cdf)
   bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)
   csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose,force=force)
   setCdf(csBC, cdf)
   qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
   csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose,force=force) #time required
   setCdf(csN, cdf)
   if (doExon)
     plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN,mergeGroups=doMerge)
   else
     plm <- RmaPlm(csN)
   fit(plm, verbose=verbose,units=NULL) #time required
   qam <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
   chp<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
   d<-NULL; ws<-NULL; rs<-NULL
   if (getExpression) {
     if (!doExon | doMerge)
       d<-getExprs(chp,doExon=F)
     else
       d<-getExprs(chp,doExon=T)
   }
   if (doResiduals)
     rs<-calculateResiduals(plm,verbose=verbose,force=force)
   if (doWeights)
     ws<-calculateWeights(plm,verbose=verbose,force=force)

list(name=name,chip=chip,d=d,cs=csN,cdf=cdf,plm=plm,qam=qam,chp=chp,res=rs,wts=ws)
}

You don't specify exactly how you call doEverything(), and what chip
type you are using ( MoEx-1_0-st or MoGene-1_0-st-v1?) but this is
certainly due the issue that in the CDF used there are a few units
that have >1000 probes each, cf. thread 'Summerization Speed Under
Unix' starting July 17, 2007, cf.

 http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/f58b942da77d48d6

In that case MoEx-1_0-st-v1 was used.  You basically want to identify
and exclude those big units from the fit.  There is currently no way
to do this with doEverything().  See also Section 'More efficient
model fitting with hundreds of variables' at

 http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/optimization-speed-file-space-ram

which also show some code that you can use to identify large units, or
the other way around, identify the set of reasonably-sized units.
Let's call the latter integer vector 'units', then you call:

  fit(plm, units=units, verbose=verbose)

in order to just fit those.

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi Dick,
If you are running the Exon Array (my personal experience) with just
the core probesets, the running time is slow for just 12 arrays, but
perhaps not in the category that some of the posts Henrik refers to. I
ran recently on a machine with 16GB memory the plm to fit the gene-
level estimates for Mark's Ensembl genes (about 20,000) on 53 chips
and it took about 40 minutes (.10sec/array)
   #20071210 23:19:45| Total time for all units across all 53 arrays:
2346.98s == 39
    #.12min
    #20071210 23:19:45| Total time per unit across all 53 arrays:
0.10s/unit
    #20071210 23:19:45| Total time per unit and array: 1.85ms/unit &
array
    #20071210 23:19:45| Total time for one array (23885 units):
0.74min = 0.01h
    #20071210 23:19:45| Total time for complete data set: 39.12min =
0.65h
    #20071210 23:19:45| Fraction of time spent on different tasks:
Fitting: 83.0%, Re
    #ading: 9.4%, Writing: 7.4% (of which 79.43% is for encoding/
writing chip-effects
    #), Explicit garbage collection: 0.2%
    #20071210 23:19:45|Fitting model of class ExonRmaPlm:...done
Fitting to the exons (merge=F) took less time (30 minutes); residuals
were very fast (<10minutes!) and weights were about 40minues. I don't
have the time on the earlier steps (bg and qn), but I would guess that
the overall time was between 2 and 3 hours. But this was a very fast
machine. I have run on my home machine (for the core probesets) and
certain steps (e.g. residuals) took much longer because the memory was
low. For the fitting, for plm fitting of the exons (merge=F) it took
an hour instead of 30 minutes for the same set of arrays; I no longer
have the output for my home machine on the gene-level fitting, but I
think it's generally longer because of the bigger sets of probes given
to the fitting.

If you are running off of Affymetrix's default chip, you probably
shouldn't! Unless you are really interested in mRNAs that don't map to
the genome, use one of the probesets I made available
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/affymetrix-defined-transcript-clusters
You can still get probeset summaries by choosing mergeGroups=FALSE.
Affy's has these ridiculously long probesets (10,000+ probes) that are
not part of the exon design but various gridding probes and other
controls. Those are the ones referred to in the post Henrik linked to.
In addition it's not binary, so if you didn't convert it, it would be
very slow reading it.

Best,
Elizabeth

Version: 0.6.2 [2007-09-07]
o Now setCdf() of AffymetrixCelSet throws an (informative) error message
  whenever one tries to use an ASCII CDF file. This behavior can be

The FirmaModel takes a ProbeLevelModel as its input, call it 'plm'.
The getDataSet() method for FirmaModel returns the what
getDataSet(plm) returns, which is the input to the PLM, *not* the
output.  That explains what you are observing.

So, instead of having FirmaModel carrying down tags from
getDataSet(plm), you wish to get the tags from getChipEffectSet(plm),
correct?

messages.body_plain:
I don't think it would be a hard thing at all, though it takes a while
and a lot of memory to make all of them (on berkeley servers, they
take about a week to create all 4 of them, but the smaller ones are
done in a day or two). I have code that takes as input the NetAffx
data (or other similar file with one entry per *probeset*) and
converts the default Affy cdf into one with the nested exon/gene
structure. In fact, my current version is in aroma.affymetrix.tools
that you set up for Mark and I to put trial functions in -- and Mark
has used it successfully, so that's good. Can anyone source a function
in from there?
Best,
Elizabeth

>
> Version: 0.6.2 [2007-09-07]
> o Now setCdf() of AffymetrixCelSet throws an (informative) error message
>   whenever one tries to use an ASCII CDF file. This behavior can be
>   changed by setting rule 'aroma.affymetrix.settings$rules$allowAsciiCdfs'
>   to TRUE in the options. The reason is that working with ASCII CDF files
>   is extremely slow and memory inefficient. Use affxparser::convertCdf()
>   to convert a CDF into a binary format.

> setCdf() is called internally when setting up a CEL set, so

>
> > > Here is the version of doEverything:
>
> > > doEverything<-function(name,chip,checkChipType=FALSE,
>
> > > doExon=FALSE,doCore=FALSE,force=FALSE,doMerge=FALSE,doResiduals=FALSE,
> > >  doWeights=FALSE,getExpression=FALSE,verbose=Arguments$getVerbose(-8))
> > > {
>
> > >    cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chip,
> > > checkChipType=checkChipType)
> > >    if (doCore)
> > >      chip<-paste(chip,",core",sep="")
> > >    cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chip)
> > >    setCdf(cs, cdf)
> > >    bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)
> > >    csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose,force=force)
> > >    setCdf(csBC, cdf)
> > >    qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
> > >    csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose,force=force) #time required
> > >    setCdf(csN, cdf)
> > >    if (doExon)
> > >      plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN,mergeGroups=doMerge)
> > >    else
> > >      plm <- RmaPlm(csN)
> > >    fit(plm, verbose=verbose,units=NULL) #time required
> > >    qam <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
> > >    chp<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
> > >    d<-NULL; ws<-NULL; rs<-NULL
> > >    if (getExpression) {
> > >      if (!doExon | doMerge)
> > >        d<-getExprs(chp,doExon=F)
> > >      else
> > >        d<-getExprs(chp,doExon=T)
> > >    }
> > >    if (doResiduals)
> > >      rs<-calculateResiduals(plm,verbose=verbose,force=force)
> > >    if (doWeights)
> > >      ws<-calculateWeights(plm,verbose=verbose,force=force)
>
> > > list(name=name,chip=chip,d=d,cs=csN,cdf=cdf,plm=plm,qam=qam,chp=chp,res=rs,wts=ws)

On Dec 13, 2007 8:41 AM, Henrik Bengtsson <h...@stat.berkeley.edu > wrote:
>
> Hi.
>
> On Dec 13, 2007 7:45 AM,  dbe...@u.washington.edu <rpb...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > Hi all,
> >
> > I just did a doEverything() call (code by Mark Robinson, thanks very
> > much).   I have 12 Mouse ST arrays.  The call took 3.76 hrs, nearly
> > all of this time was due to the fit(plm) step (plm is the output from
> > RmaPlm).  Does that seem like a usual length of time to anyone?
>
> You don't specify exactly how you call doEverything(), and what chip
> type you are using ( MoEx-1_0-st or MoGene-1_0-st-v1?) but this is
> certainly due the issue that in the CDF used there are a few units
> that have >1000 probes each, cf. thread 'Summerization Speed Under
> Unix' starting July 17, 2007, cf.
>
>  http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/f58b942da77d48d6
>
> In that case MoEx-1_0-st-v1 was used.  You basically want to identify
> and exclude those big units from the fit.  There is currently no way
> to do this with doEverything().  See also Section 'More efficient
> model fitting with hundreds of variables' at
>
>  http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/optimization-speed-file-space-ram
>
> which also show some code that you can use to identify large units, or
> the other way around, identify the set of reasonably-sized units.
> Let's call the latter integer vector 'units', then you call:
>
>  fit(plm, units=units, verbose=verbose)
>
> in order to just fit those.
>
> Hope this helps
>
> Henrik
>
> >
> >  Total time for all units across all 12 arrays: 13522.67s == 225.38min
> >  Total time per unit across all 12 arrays: 0.38s/unit
> >  Total time per unit and array: 31.7ms/unit & array
> >  Total time for one array (35512 units): 18.78min = 0.31h
> >  Total time for complete data set: 225.38min = 3.76h
> >  Fraction of time spent on different tasks: Fitting: 99.3%, Reading:
> > 0.1%, Writing: 0.6% (of which 75.19% is for encoding/writing chip-
> > effects), Explicit garbage collection: 0.0%
> >
> >
> > Here is the version of doEverything:
> >
> > doEverything<-function(name,chip,checkChipType=FALSE,
> >
> > doExon=FALSE,doCore=FALSE,force=FALSE,doMerge=FALSE,doResiduals=FALSE,
> >  doWeights=FALSE,getExpression=FALSE,verbose=Arguments$getVerbose(-8))
> > {
> >
> >    cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chip,
> > checkChipType=checkChipType)
> >    if (doCore)
> >      chip<-paste(chip,",core",sep="")
> >    cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chip)
> >    setCdf(cs, cdf)
> >    bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)
> >    csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose,force=force)
> >    setCdf(csBC, cdf)
> >    qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
> >    csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose,force=force) #time required
> >    setCdf(csN, cdf)
> >    if (doExon)
> >      plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN,mergeGroups=doMerge)
> >    else
> >      plm <- RmaPlm(csN)
> >    fit(plm, verbose=verbose,units=NULL) #time required
> >    qam <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
> >    chp<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
> >    d<-NULL; ws<-NULL; rs<-NULL
> >    if (getExpression) {
> >      if (!doExon | doMerge)
> >        d<-getExprs(chp,doExon=F)
> >      else
> >        d<-getExprs(chp,doExon=T)
> >    }
> >    if (doResiduals)
> >      rs<-calculateResiduals(plm,verbose=verbose,force=force)
> >    if (doWeights)
> >      ws<-calculateWeights(plm,verbose=verbose,force=force)
> >
> > list(name=name,chip=chip,d=d,cs=csN,cdf=cdf,plm=plm,qam=qam,chp=chp,res=rs,wts=ws)

messages.subject: Re: problem with Firma tags
messages.body_plain:
Hi Henrik,
I think that it is better to carry the tags from
getChipEffectSet(plm). True, right now you *have* to run the RMA,
merged=T to have residuals or weights, so it's a bit redundant, but
conceivably there might be another model fitting that gave residuals
that you would use (or someone will use FIRMA very oddly on something
else). Also, I'd like the tags to carry through as a documentation of
the analysis, regardless if there doesn't seem to be a choice about
running a particular step. There's always the possibility that there
was a choice made by the user, like changing the cdf or rerunning
under different versions of something that the tags could indicate.
Thanks,
Elizabeth

Hi,

So I was mucking around in the extractMatrix commands to make one for
firma output -- which is basically a non-existant necessity because
Henrik's done all the work. The only problem is 1) getDataFlat doesn't
return 'theta' and 'sdtheta' for the headers for FirmaSet, so I have
to switch those (it would be better to have it replace in getDataFlat,
as it does in the other functions so that they are all the same) and

copy the function and rename it! So thanks Henrik. By the way, is
there a way to *not* copy the function so if there are updates both
don't have to be updated (obviously nextMethod won't work). Since the
only difference is the headers from 'getDataFlat' couldn't there be a
generic (AffymetrixCelSet) method so that only getDataFlat had to be
specific? I guess there would have to be a getDataFlat method for
