> On 11/12/2007, Elizabeth Purdom <epur...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>
>
> > Hello,
>
> > Someone showed me some example code that is posted online for lbl (not
> > on the group pages) to get a ngene x nchip matrix of the expression
> > values from a ExonRmaPlm fitting and it has a serious mistake. I don't
> > know where the code came from or who might be using it, so I thought I'd
> > point it out on the list. The code is roughly,
>
> > plm <- ExonRmaPlm(cs, mergeGroups=TRUE);
> > ces <- getChipEffects(plm);
> > chipEffectMatrix <- getData(ces, indices=NULL, "intensities")$intensities
> > cdf <- getCdf(ces);
> > groupNames <- readCdfGroupNames(cdf$.pathname, truncateGroupNames=FALSE);
> > chipEffectMatrix <- chipEffectMatrix[1:length(unlist(groupNames)),];
>
> > I just wanted to point out that this will not give the chip (gene)
> > effects, which is quite clear if you look at the first few lines of the
> > matrix.
>
> > The main mistake is in the last line, (though I can't vouch for the
> > other without double-checking it). In general, the 'getData' function
> > pulls data from every cell on the .CEL file as defined by the
> > corresponding cdf. The chip effects have a cdf (called a 'monocell' cdf)
> > that has a reduced number of cells, only 1 cell (entry) per every group
> > per unit on the original cdf, rather than per probe. For the ExonRmaPlm,
> > when mergeGroups=T only one value is needed per unit, so only one group
> > per unit has a value and the rest are zero. The last line of the above
> > code tries to get rid of these zero entries, but it is not that simple
> > since the nonzero ones are not the first ngene rows of the matrix.
>
> > Generally, I'm always a bit hesitant to use functions that need the
> > indices without extreme care because I don't think that the indices must
> > always go in the order of the units (except for the monocell, isn't the
> > index the position on the array of the probe, irrelevant to the
> > group/unit definitions?). In which case, getData would give you a matrix
> > with no way of mapping back to the names. However, the monocell is more
> > standard since its created by aroma.affymetrix for the sole purpose of
> > holding chip effects and is based on the cdf, not the probe positions;
> > just looking at the first few entries, it seems like the monocell might
> > have the indices and units that line up in the same order. In which case
> > this code could probably be fixed if instead it used
> > readCdfNbrOfCellsPerUnitGroup() and calculated the appropriate index in
> > that way. I'd stick with readUnits(), however and collapse the list
> > structure into a matrix (something I was thinking of coding myself since
> > I don't know of a function that does it, or maybe writing code based on
> > getData that made sure everything lined up and gave the names, because I
> > think getData would be faster).
>
> > The code above should give exon summaries, if plm was from
> > mergeGroups=FALSE, but then it would have the same issues of mapping
> > from indices to units/groups. If the monocell is in the 'right' order,
> > then the code would give the entries in the same order as
> > unlist(groupNames), so you could map back to the probeset ids in that way.
>
> > As a development question, if you want such a collapsed matrix for a set
> > of units, would it be faster to look up the appropriate indices (with
> > getCellIndices) and then use getData, or use readUnits and then use
> > matrix() on the output of unlist()? (Obviously for the chip effects,
> > this would have to be adjusted for the zeros, and readUnits leaves them
> > out automatically so that is more convenient)
>
> > Best,
> > Elizabeth

On Dec 13, 2007 1:36 PM, epurdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> So I was mucking around in the extractMatrix commands to make one for
> firma output -- which is basically a non-existant necessity because
> Henrik's done all the work. The only problem is 1) getDataFlat doesn't
> return 'theta' and 'sdtheta' for the headers for FirmaSet, so I have
> to switch those (it would be better to have it replace in getDataFlat,
> as it does in the other functions so that they are all the same) and
> 2) FirmaSet doesn't actually inherit from ChipEffectSet so I have to
> copy the function and rename it! So thanks Henrik. By the way, is
> there a way to *not* copy the function so if there are updates both
> don't have to be updated (obviously nextMethod won't work).  Since the
> only difference is the headers from 'getDataFlat' couldn't there be a
> generic (AffymetrixCelSet) method so that only getDataFlat had to be
> specific? I guess there would have to be a getDataFlat method for
> AffymetrixCelSet (though there's already one for residual/weight cel
> files which are similar beasts, I thought)
>

First, getDataFlat() only exist for NnnFile classes at this moment,
not for NnnSet classes (another thing on my tooodooo list).  Instead
we let extractMatrix() call getDataFlat() for each file and build up
the matrix.

Second, yes, instead of cut'n'pasting the code from one class to
another, you can instead take the existing code, generalize it, and
"lift it up" in a superclass.  Then modify the existing method so it
calls NextMethod() with some extra arguments, say, fields="theta" or
field="intensities".

For your problem, I would start doing this for the getDataFlat()
method.  The common superclass of ChipEffectFile, FirmaFile,
ResidualFile, and WeightFile is ParameterCelFile.  Then
extractMatrix() should be an easy task to generalize.

/Henrik

/Henrik

> > On 11/12/2007, Elizabeth Purdom <epur...@gmail.com> wrote:

> >
> >
> > > Hello,
> >
> > > Someone showed me some example code that is posted online for lbl (not
> > > on the group pages) to get a ngene x nchip matrix of the expression
> > > values from a ExonRmaPlm fitting and it has a serious mistake. I don't
> > > know where the code came from or who might be using it, so I thought I'd
> > > point it out on the list. The code is roughly,
> >
> > > plm <- ExonRmaPlm(cs, mergeGroups=TRUE);
> > > ces <- getChipEffects(plm);
> > > chipEffectMatrix <- getData(ces, indices=NULL, "intensities")$intensities
> > > cdf <- getCdf(ces);
> > > groupNames <- readCdfGroupNames(cdf$.pathname, truncateGroupNames=FALSE);
> > > chipEffectMatrix <- chipEffectMatrix[1:length(unlist(groupNames)),];
> >
> > > I just wanted to point out that this will not give the chip (gene)
> > > effects, which is quite clear if you look at the first few lines of the
> > > matrix.
> >
> > > The main mistake is in the last line, (though I can't vouch for the
> > > other without double-checking it). In general, the 'getData' function
> > > pulls data from every cell on the .CEL file as defined by the
> > > corresponding cdf. The chip effects have a cdf (called a 'monocell' cdf)
> > > that has a reduced number of cells, only 1 cell (entry) per every group
> > > per unit on the original cdf, rather than per probe. For the ExonRmaPlm,
> > > when mergeGroups=T only one value is needed per unit, so only one group
> > > per unit has a value and the rest are zero. The last line of the above
> > > code tries to get rid of these zero entries, but it is not that simple
> > > since the nonzero ones are not the first ngene rows of the matrix.
> >
> > > Generally, I'm always a bit hesitant to use functions that need the
> > > indices without extreme care because I don't think that the indices must
> > > always go in the order of the units (except for the monocell, isn't the
> > > index the position on the array of the probe, irrelevant to the
> > > group/unit definitions?). In which case, getData would give you a matrix
> > > with no way of mapping back to the names. However, the monocell is more
> > > standard since its created by aroma.affymetrix for the sole purpose of
> > > holding chip effects and is based on the cdf, not the probe positions;
> > > just looking at the first few entries, it seems like the monocell might
> > > have the indices and units that line up in the same order. In which case
> > > this code could probably be fixed if instead it used
> > > readCdfNbrOfCellsPerUnitGroup() and calculated the appropriate index in
> > > that way. I'd stick with readUnits(), however and collapse the list
> > > structure into a matrix (something I was thinking of coding myself since
> > > I don't know of a function that does it, or maybe writing code based on
> > > getData that made sure everything lined up and gave the names, because I
> > > think getData would be faster).
> >
> > > The code above should give exon summaries, if plm was from
> > > mergeGroups=FALSE, but then it would have the same issues of mapping
> > > from indices to units/groups. If the monocell is in the 'right' order,
> > > then the code would give the entries in the same order as
> > > unlist(groupNames), so you could map back to the probeset ids in that way.
> >
> > > As a development question, if you want such a collapsed matrix for a set
> > > of units, would it be faster to look up the appropriate indices (with
> > > getCellIndices) and then use getData, or use readUnits and then use
> > > matrix() on the output of unlist()? (Obviously for the chip effects,
> > > this would have to be adjusted for the zeros, and readUnits leaves them
> > > out automatically so that is more convenient)
> >
> > > Best,
> > > Elizabeth
> >
>

keep much track on those classes, and when I do, I always have single
group cases.  These files was written by Ken who obviously is not
watching them (since he left).

Have a look at the getCellMap() methods for the problematic classes.
That method should return the (unit, group, cell) map given what
getCellIndices() of the same class is returning.  Note, the latter is
the one deciding what groups to return given, say, argument
'mergeGroups'.  When I recently said I patched extractMatrix(), the
main bug fix was indeed in getCellMap() for ChipEffectFile (on the
SVN).  So, that's a good start/template.

Cheers

/Henrik

Forgot to mention.  One thing one can do to lower the risk for bugs in
the future, is to add a small script testing for detected bug/buglet.
Then I can easily add that to the redundancy tests I run between
releases.  The more tests the higher quality.

So, anyone/everyone, if you a find bug, please try to provide a short
as possible code snippet asserting its correctness so that I can add
it to the set of test scripts.  It is good if works out of one of the
vignettes online.

Cheers

Henrik

I may/may not understand what you want.  So, basically here is the
format that getTags() returns:

  <output tags> := <input data set tags>,<constructor tags>

where <constructor tags> defaults to "*" (argument 'tags' in
constructor).  There is currently no way to override/remove the <input
data set tags>, but only the <constructor tags>.  So, please don't
change the above rule/defintion, because that is a general pattern of
aroma.affymetrix.

For clarification, if specifying an asterisk in <constructor tags>,
e.g. tags="*,main", the asterisk tag is replaced with what
getAsteriskTags() is return.  The latter returns tags that specify the
transform/model plus its parameters, e.g. for RmaCnPlm(...,
combineAlleles=TRUE, tags="*,foo") we get "RMA,A+B" from
getAsteriskTags() and "foo" from the remainder, such that:

<constructor tags>="RMA,A+B,foo"

in the above.

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Affy SNP 6.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

That error tells us that the valid range of units is "[1,1856069]".
Now, that (1,856,069) is exactly then number of units in the default
CDF, i.e. GenomeWideSNP_6.cdf that comes along with
GenomeWideSNP_6.Full.cdf.  The full CDF has 1,881,415 units.

Basically, hide away GenomeWideSNP_6.cdf or similar, because you won't
need it, and make sure you only got GenomeWideSNP_6.Full.cdf, which
you have to rename to have ",Full" instead of ".Full".

I suspect somehow the default CDF was mistakenly used by
aroma.affymetrix, instead of the full CDF.  I have a vague memory of
seeing a similar side effect while I was modifying the package to
better deal with tags and custom CDFs.  It might be that the v0.8.0
you have got that buglet.  Update aroma.affymetrix!  Things are moving
fast.

Then, use the (updated) example code in:

  http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis-6-0

which recently have been confirmed to work by another user.

Let us know if this helps, and if not, please show us the complete
script you are using.

Cheers

Henrik

the only problem might be that your chip-effect CEL files' headers are
specifying the wrong chip type.  So, what does you get if you do?

# Raw data
str(getHeader(getFile(cs,1)))

# Calibrated data
str(getHeader(getFile(csC,1)))

# Chip effects
str(getHeader(getFile(ces,1)))

# Normalized chip effects
str(getHeader(getFile(cesN,1)))

It might be a very simple thing.

/Henrik

On 17/12/2007, mbc...@gmail.com <mbc...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Or, I should just include everything in 1 analysis?  To give you a

It is hard to tell without doing a serious QC analysis, but my
experience is that you can quite safely combine data over time,
especially if they come out of the same microarray facility.

>
> In addition, when I calculate the CN, what would be a good reference
> for unpaired tumor samples?
> I am thinking about using the average of all the control samples
> (including both the  paired and unpaired controls),
> what do you think?

How many hybridizations do you have?  Does the tumors have a lot of
aberrations, or just a few randomly located?   If you have enough
normals, just use them, but if only have say 10 or less, you can try
to include a few tumors that are "not too wild" and consistent.  The
assumption is that at any random locus the majority of samples are
copy neutral.

/Henrik

Which CDF do you use for your GWS5 analysis?  The UFL files provided
are for the "full" (and "alternative") CDF called
GenomeWideSNP_5.Full.r2.cdf.  It does not match the units in the
"default" CDF, e.g. GenomeWideSNP_5.cdf or the "default/alternative"
GenomeWideSNP_5.r2.cdf.

My best guess from your output is that you are using the "default" CDF
named GenomeWideSNP_5.cdf (or possibly GenomeWideSNP_5.r2.cdf), and in
such cases aroma.affymetrix cannot find a corresponding UFL file
(you'll have the same problem later with the UGP file).

Are you aware of vignette "Total Copy Number Analysis (5.0 & 6.0)"?  See

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis-6-0

Make sure to follow to follow the instructions under "Annotation data"
carefully.  Especially the part saying that you need to rename
"GenomeWideSNP_5.Full.r2.cdf" to "GenomeWideSNP_5,Full,r2.cdf" (note
commas).  I know this is a little bit annoying having to rename files
like this.  I am trying to come up with a safe  way for
aroma.affymetrix to recognize both version, but until then you have to
rename the files.

>
>

> ##returns

> SNP5_snp_info.txt
> File size: 3.51MB
> RAM: 0.00MB
> Chip type: GenomeWideSNP_5

No, that will not work.  Now aroma.affymetrix thinks the file is of
the dChip file format.  I am actually surprised that aroma.affymetrix
does not throw an exception - at least it should when later try to use
it.

Basically, you should *never* ever have to do hacks such a renaming
annotation files to get things working, that is, unless I explicitly
have written so somewhere (as in the above case, but that's rare).  In
other words, it is better to ask for help when you're in doubt, as you
did.

If you follow the above vignette, it should work smoothly.  In that
vignette the validity of the UFL and UGP files are tested before you
start your analysis.  Let me know if it helps.

For future correspondence, please provide your sessionInfo() output.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v0.8.3 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

aroma.affymetrix v0.8.3 is available.  Here are the details:

Version: 0.8.3 [2007-12-18]
o UPDATE: Package patches installed by downloadPackagePatch()
  are now stored in ~/.Rpatches/ (previously in ./patches/).
  Thus, patches will be applied regardless of working directory.
o UPDATE: Changed fit() for FirmaModel to operate as fit() for
  ProbeLevelModel, where the units are read in in chunks and
  operated on over all chips, instead reading and operating
  chip-by-chip.  Default summary is now the median residual
  instead of 1-UQR of weights.  The added tags will reflect what
  settings are used.
o DEVEL: Added summaryOfUnits() for AromaUflFile.
o BUG FIX: extractMatrix() of ChipEffectSet was broken (due to an
  internal bug in getCellMap() of ChipEffectFile).
o BUG FIX: When calling fit() on a ProbeLevelModel for chip type
  where no monocell CDF exists, an exception like "Could not create
  AffymetrixCdfFile object. No CDF file with that chip type found:
  GenomeWideSNP_6,Full,monocell" would be thrown.  This is due to
  a bug introduced in previous version when trying to make sure
  custom CDFs are carried down more consistently.  Now getMonoCell()
  of AffymetrixCdfFile will create the monocell CDF, if missing.

See website for update instructions.

Best,

Henrik

messages.subject: Re: saving workspace output from aroma.affymetrix
messages.body_plain:
Hi Christina.

On 21/12/2007, Christina Curtis <ccu...@usc.edu> wrote:
> Hi Henrik,
>
> First off, aroma.affymetrix is of great utility, so many thanks for this excellent tool.
> I was in doubt that this question would be relevant to others so thought I should just email you directly.

I took the freedom to continue this on the aroma.affymetrix mailing
list.  Please post *all* aroma.affymetrix questions there.  It might
help someone else and the archive helps me to at least refer back to
previous similar issues.

>
> I am wondering how best to access and reload the important R objects and files after having pre-processed data using aroma once an R session has been ended?
> The reason I am concerned is that I have now had two crashes, the most recent one occurred when trying to output some plots following segmentation with cbs. Now, I have the option of how to end my R session. Normally, I would just exit R saving the workspace, but in my experience with aroma. affymetrix, when I save the workspace and try to reload most of my objects are no longer there (say if I type ls()). As such, I have now spent multiple hours pre-processing the data and I can see that I now have probeData, plmData and even a little cbsData, but am not sure how to "reload" it ALL into my workspace so that I can continue with the downstream analysis eg) segmentation.

In general, all results in all steps in the analysis you have done are
stored in persistent memory, that is, on the file system.  The methods
are designed to detect already processed results such that the
corresponding computations don't have to be redone.  This happens
automatically.  In other words, if you just rerun the same steps, it
should be fairly fast.  There are some parts that still take a little
bit of time, but that should be marginal compared to the full
analysis.

Personally I never save workspaces to .RData but rather rerun scripts.
 The main reason for this is that parts of the .RData files are likely
to become incompatible with package updates.  When I updated
aroma.affymetrix I do NOT consider the case that the contents of an
**in-memory object** saved in an earlier version of the package might
get reloaded later on.  I simply cannot write code that is backward
compatible with all possible versions of the package. Note, this is
not to say that the stored results under probeData/, plmData/ etc are
not backward compatible - they are.

>
> Would it be better to "abort (with core dump)" this time?

To the problem of R crashing:
This is a scenario that we should never end up with so there is no
guideline for what is best.  However, it is alway advisable to end a
corrupt R session and since all results are persistent between R
sessions it should in most cases not affect your aroma.affymetrix
analysis.

To the cause of R crashing:
You wrote "...I have now had two crashes, the most recent one occurred
when trying to output some plots following segmentation with cbs".
You should not expect R to crash so when it happens, please report it
with as much details as possible.  At least it is good to track down
which package might be the cause.

>
> Surely, there must be a way to avoid loading all the individual .Rdata files for each chip?
> Can I export a single file for use with different segmentation tools - cbs / GLAD, snapCGH, SNPchip, aCGH etc?

I'll reply to this in your follow up.

>
> Error:

>  *** caught segfault ***
> address 0x352c1000, cause 'memory not mapped'
> ........
> ........
> ........
>
> Possible actions:
> 1: abort (with core dump, if enabled)
> 2: normal R exit
> 3: exit R without saving workspace
> 4: exit R saving workspace

The information "address 0x352c1000, cause 'memory not mapped'" gives
me no clues alone, but with the exact call and verbose output it
should be possible to narrow down the source.

>
>
> If I reload a previously saved workspace that I generated in the middle of pre-processing just as a safeguard:
>
> >load("SNP5.0_Run.Rdata")
>
> Attempting to load the environment 'package:R.utils'

On 21/12/2007, Christina Curtis <ccu...@usc.edu> wrote:

> I am still not sure whether many QC functions are in place (similar to those available in the affy/oligo  package) for these arrays as I did encounter an error in trying to obtain the residuals from the probe-level model fit.

There are only a few QC methods implemented in aroma.affymetrix and
the ones available are documented/illustrated under Section "User's
Guide" online.  Contributions are welcomed.

>
>  Lastly, I am trying to determine the best way to save the data in a text file that I can upload for use with various segmentation tools - cbs / GLAD, snapCGH, SNPchip, aCGH etc.

> You mention that cbs is the fastest- have you also input this type of data into any of the HMM algorithms?

I mean that CBS is faster than GLAD.  There are also some other
segmentation methods for which it is obvious that CBS is faster from
just looking at the described model/algorithm and the quality of
implementation.  Also, different segmentation methods do different
things so it is not always fair to compare them.

See Vignette "Calculating raw total copy numbers manually" online how
the obtain raw CNs as a standard R matrix.  See R documentation how to
save such data to file and so on.

The class structure of the segmentation model classes, e.g. CbsModel
and GladModel and super class CopyNumberSegmentationModel, has be
designed to simplify the process of adding support for other
segmentation methods.  If you look at the source for, say, CbsModel
you'll find that it doesn't take much code to write a wrapper for the
aCGH method.

Best,

Henrik
